stem: Why are the DNA copies made in a reproducing cell similar to, but not always identical to, the original?

The environment adds new DNA to every copy.

stem: Why can a reproducing cell not simply keep one DNA copy and push the other copy out of the cell?

The pushed-out copy would contain twice the normal amount of DNA.
The original cell would lose all of its proteins at once.
The pushed-out copy would fuse at once with another cell.

stem: In some sections of society the child sex ratio is falling at an alarming rate even though prenatal sex determination is banned by law. What does the chapter identify as the cause?
options: The rising use of oral pills that cause side effects
Sexually transmitted diseases affecting girls more
Reckless female foeticide through illegal abortions
A natural fall in the number of eggs released yearly
explanation: Correct option: (C). The chapter points to illegal sex-selective abortion of female foetuses (female foeticide) as the reason the child sex ratio is declining, and stresses that a healthy society needs a balanced female-male sex ratio. Side effects of pills, STDs and egg release are not given as causes of a falling child sex ratio.
